source_fields.formulation: Minimize simultaneous coordinate regret for a two-objective lexicographic stochastic bandit without a supplied tradeoff envelope.

assumptions.description: The public arm space $(\mathcal X,D)$ is a nonempty compact metric space with diameter at most one. The two means take values in [0,1] and are 1-Lipschitz. Compactness ensures the lexicographic optimum exists.
assumptions.scope: The domain stated in this clause.

assumptions.description: There are two fixed reward means $\mu^1,\mu^2$ taking values in $[0,1]$. The primary optimum set is $\mathcal X_1^*=\arg\max_x\mu^1(x)$, and a lexicographic optimum $x^*$ maximizes $\mu^2$ over that set. Primary ties are permitted.
assumptions.scope: The domain stated in this clause.

assumptions.description: The local tradeoff is $\lambda_* =\inf\{\lambda\ge0:\mu^2(x)-\mu^2(x^*)\le\lambda[\mu^1(x^*)-\mu^1(x)]\ \forall x\}$. No value or upper bound for $\lambda_*$ is supplied. The same policy must handle all admissible means without such side information.
assumptions.scope: The domain stated in this clause.

assumptions.description: The local tradeoff can be infinite on compact infinite spaces. The main no-envelope guarantees hold on this class and their lower bounds also hold on the finite-tradeoff subclass.
assumptions.scope: The domain stated in this clause.

source_fields.operation: At round $t$, choose an arm $X_t$ using the past and an independent random seed; then observe both coordinates $(Y_t^1,Y_t^2)$. Each coordinate is conditionally 1-sub-Gaussian around its fixed mean: $\mathbb E[\exp(\theta(Y_t^i-\mu^i(X_t)))\mid\mathcal H_{t-1},X_t]\le\exp(\theta^2/2)$. Independence between coordinates is not required. There is no feedback for unselected arms and no sample reuse interface. The horizon and metric are public. A measurable maximal-net oracle, given a nonempty compact subset U and r>0, returns a finite inclusion-maximal r-separated subset. Its computational cost is not charged as a reward observation. Mean functions, primary ties, and near-optimality packing parameters are hidden; the policy uses no tradeoff envelope.

feedback_quality.description: The conditional law and exact response packet are specified in the oracle paragraphs.

operations.query_signature: The query domain and ordering stated in the oracle paragraphs.

source_fields.feasibility: The output is the sequence of selected arms. One policy must control both objective regrets against the same lexicographic optimum.

source_fields.base_expression: Define $\Delta_i(x)=\mu^i(x^*)-\mu^i(x)$ and signed coordinate regret $R_i(T)=\sum_{t=1}^T\Delta_i(X_t)$. The simultaneous expected criterion is $\max_{i\le2}\mathbb E R_i(T)$. The secondary regret can be negative, so the maximum is taken after each expectation.

source_fields.budget: There is one arm pull and two scalar reward observations per round, so the fixed horizon is $T$, the pull count is $T$, and the number of observed reward coordinates is $2T$. Computation and storage are unrestricted. Metric-net computation and reward samples are separate resources. The comparison is information theoretic and does not charge the net construction.
